keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Lower Nubia between the First and Second Cataracts (134 land cells, about 33,902 km2 after trimming; the gazetteer's Lower Nubia has 188), the A-Group page's own range; the page says it "flourished between the First and Second Cataracts" and that "Early hubs of this civilization included Kubaniyya in the north and Buhen in the south". No area is given.

ledger.note: 3500 BCE: the Early A-Group culture arises in Lower Nubia. "Around 3500 BC, the second 'Nubian' culture, termed the Early A-Group culture, arose in Lower Nubia." (The A-Group page says only "from the 4th millennium BC".)
3100 BCE: the A-Group reaches its Classical phase. "Around 3100 BC, the A-group transitioned from the Early to Classical phases"; the A-Group page: "reached its climax at c. 3100 BC".

region.text: "located in modern northern Sudan and southern Egypt and flourished between the First and Second Cataracts"; "the Early A-Group culture, arose in Lower Nubia"; less the Nile band that naqada-culture draws and the Cliopatria Early Dynastic Egypt shape of -3000, which both reach south of the First Cataract in the gazetteer

ledger.note: 2900 BCE: the A-Group falls. "It lasted from the 4th millennium BC, reached its climax at c. 3100 BC, and fell 200 years later c. 2900 BC"; the Nubia page: "came to an end sometime between 3100 and 2900 BC", "apparently destroyed by the First Dynasty rulers of Egypt". The page does not say Egypt took the land, so it passes to nobody; Reisner's B-Group and C-Group are said to follow.

certainty.note: A river-valley culture known from cemeteries; no border is recorded.

notes: A-Group culture, Lower Nubia. The A-Group page has no infobox and says the culture "lasted beyond 3100 BC" against Reisner's original end (3100). The Nubia page supplies the start (3500). Early Dynastic Egypt (early-dynastic-period-of-egypt, me-03) is the northern neighbour from c. 3150; the Nubia page says it "apparently destroyed" the A-Group, which is not a transfer of land. Naqada (Upper Egypt, naqada-culture) borders it at Aswan; the overlap with Naqada and Early Dynastic Egypt was checked with the gazetteer (see the batch notes). Trimming: the gazetteer's Lower Nubia (Wawat) has 188 cells; 54 lie in the Upper Egypt Nile band of naqada-culture_-4000/-3200 and 10 in the Cliopatria Early Dynastic Egypt shape, so those are removed to keep the two dossiers disjoint, although the A-Group page puts Kubaniyya (near Aswan) and Qustul (near Abu Simbel) in the A-Group. The Egyptian group should stop the Naqada band and the Early Dynastic shape at the First Cataract (Aswan); the cells can then be restored here.
